issues.description: The problem statement and the template define a public method named singFarmSong() on Farm that students are expected to implement and use to 'play the song'. However, the solution implementation exposes this functionality under a differently named public method playFarmSong(), while keeping a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal) helper. This name/signature mismatch between template/problem and solution is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students (they will implement singFarmSong() as specified, but the solution and any reference tests based on it use playFarmSong()).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the public API consistent: rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or alternatively rename the template and update the problem statement to require playFarmSong(). Ensure the public method name used in tests, the template stub, and the problem description all match (preferably singFarmSong() as specified in the UML and tasks).

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Farm method named singFarmSong(), but the solution implementation defines playFarmSong() instead. This renaming of the core method that 'plays/sings' the farm song creates a direct mapping confusion for students (and even leaves Main referring to singFarmSong()).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() and update all internal references (e.g., Main) to use singFarmSong(), so the method name matches the problem statement and template expectation. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use playFarmSong() consistently, but prefer matching the original problem-specified name singFarmSong().
